title: The unit torus of a finite separable extension has permutation characters
statement:
Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $k^s/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and let $L/k$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension]: $L$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and the minimal polynomial of every element has distinct roots in an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. There is an affine $k$-torus $Q_L$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, def-sc-group-scheme], of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with natural group isomorphisms
$$Q_L(R)\simeq(L\otimes_k R)^\times$$
for all commutative $k$-algebras $R$, where $Q_L(R)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}R,Q_L)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], tensor products have the algebra structure of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], and $B^\times$ is the group of multiplicatively invertible elements of a ring $B$. Put $E=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(L,k^s)$ and $\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(k^s/k)$. Then the character group of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] has a $\Gamma$-equivariant identification
$$X^*(Q_L)\simeq\mathbf Z[E].$$
Here $\mathbf Z[E]$ is the free abelian group with basis $e_\sigma$, $\sigma\in E$, and $\gamma e_\sigma=e_{\gamma\circ\sigma}$. Under the natural identification $L\otimes_k k^s\simeq\prod_{\sigma\in E}k^s$, $a\otimes b\mapsto(\sigma(a)b)_\sigma$, the basis vector $e_\sigma$ corresponds to the coordinate character $((z_\tau)_\tau\mapsto z_\sigma)$. These assertions include $L=k$.

source.place: Sections 2.54--2.55, printed p.57 (represented group functor); 2.59--2.61, printed pp.58--59 (scalar extension and splitting); Lemma 12.61, printed p.251 (permutation character module). Affineness also follows from the affine restriction construction, Stacks Tag 0BL3, lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine, more-morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Choose a finite $k$-basis of $L$; its size $d$ is positive since $L$ is a field. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-algebra-units-affine-chart] with $A=L$. It gives $U=D(N)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, and natural bijections $U(R)\simeq(L\otimes_kR)^\times$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b), $U=\operatorname{Spec}B_N$. The localization presentation [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] gives $B_N\simeq B[t]/(Nt-1)$, generated over $k$ by $x_1,\ldots,x_d,t$. Thus the one affine chart of $U$ is finitely generated over $k$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] makes $U$ of finite type.

source.place: 2.54--2.55, p.57; Proposition 12.60, p.250, multiplication-matrix affine chart.

proof.text: Transport the units-group operations through the bijections in Step 1, and call the resulting group scheme $Q_L$. Here is the representability check behind the functor-of-points criterion in [def-sc-group-scheme]. In the category of affine $k$-schemes, multiplication is a natural transformation $h_{U\times_kU}\to h_U$, inversion is $h_U\to h_U$, and the constant unit is $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\to h_U$. Products stay affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Full faithfulness [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] turns these transformations into morphisms; their group identities follow from the units identities and injectivity of that same bijection on morphisms. Therefore $Q_L$ is affine of finite type and the bijections in Step 1 are natural group isomorphisms, also for nonreduced test rings.

source.place: 2.55, p.57; Proposition 3.1, p.64, represented group-valued functor.

proof.text: First, $L/k$ is separable algebraic in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Every $\beta\in L$ is algebraic, as $1,\beta,\ldots,\beta^{d}$ are linearly dependent for $d=\dim_kL$. If its minimal polynomial $\mu$ were not separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], then by [def-weil-coprime-polynomials] $\mu$ and $\mu'$ would have a nonconstant common divisor in $k[T]$, with a root $r$ in the algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Writing $\mu=(T-r)Q$ there gives $\mu'=Q+(T-r)Q'$, so $Q(r)=\mu'(r)=0$ and $r$ is a repeated root of $\mu$, contrary to the hypothesis on $L/k$. Apply [lem-zl-finite-separable-tensor-primitive-presentation] with $E=L$ and $K=k^s$. It gives $L=k(\alpha)$, the monic irreducible minimal polynomial $P\in k[T]$ of positive degree, and a $k^s$-algebra isomorphism $k^s\otimes_kL\simeq k^s[T]/(P_{k^s})$ taking $b\otimes g(\alpha)$ to $[bg(T)]$. In particular $P$ is separable. In the coprimality definition [def-pc-separable-polynomial], a Bezout identity $UP+VP'=1$ remains such an identity after coefficient extension; hence $P_{k^s}$ is separable. The field $k^s$ is separably closed by [def-pd-separable-closure], so [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization] gives $P_{k^s}=\prod_{i=1}^n(T-r_i)$. No two roots coincide: a repeated factor would make both $P_{k^s}$ and its derivative vanish at that root, contradicting the Bezout identity. Since $P$ has positive degree, $n\geq1$.

source.place: 2.61, p.59, the finite separable tensor decomposition, expanded using a primitive element.

proof.text: In $k^s[T]$ put $I_i=(T-r_i)$. For $i\ne j$, the difference of the two generators is the nonzero scalar $r_j-r_i$, so $I_i+I_j=(1)$. Their intersection equals their product: for two coprime ideals $I,J$ write $1=u+v$ with $u\in I,v\in J$, and for $x\in I\cap J$ use $x=xu+xv\in IJ$; induction gives the finite-family assertion (the product of ideals coprime to $J$ is coprime to $J$, by multiplying identities modulo $J$). Thus $\bigcap_i I_i=(P_{k^s})$. The Chinese remainder isomorphism [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] and evaluation $k^s[T]/(T-r_i)\simeq k^s$ give $k^s[T]/(P_{k^s})\simeq\prod_i k^s$, by $[g]\mapsto(g(r_i))_i$. A $k$-algebra map $L\to k^s$ is uniquely determined by the image of $\alpha$, and those images are exactly the roots of $P$: use $L\simeq k[T]/(P)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso] and the evaluation bijection [lem-asd-polynomial-quotient-hom-equivalence]. Every such map is injective since it is a unital map of fields. Reindexing by $E=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(L,k^s)$ and swapping the tensor factors therefore gives the precise algebra isomorphism $\theta:L\otimes_kk^s\simeq\prod_{\sigma\in E}k^s$, $a\otimes b\mapsto(\sigma(a)b)_\sigma$.

For a commutative $k^s$-algebra $R$, tensor associativity identifies $L\otimes_kR$ with $(L\otimes_kk^s)\otimes_{k^s}R$: the map $(a\otimes b)\otimes r\mapsto a\otimes br$ has inverse $a\otimes r\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes r$, well-defined by the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. After $\theta$, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] identifies this algebra with $\prod_{\sigma\in E}R$; its module isomorphism preserves multiplication and unit by the pure-tensor formulas. Taking units gives $(Q_L)_{k^s}(R)\simeq\prod_{\sigma\in E}R^\times$, naturally in $R$, since a tuple is invertible exactly when every coordinate is invertible. For the left side, the affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and scalar-extension adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-base-change-universal-property] identify its points with $Q_L(R)$. The right side is the point functor of $\mathbf G_m^E$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Full faithfulness [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] makes these inverse natural maps an isomorphism of group schemes. Extending the same isomorphism to an algebraic closure gives a split torus there; hence $Q_L$ is a torus by [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type].

source.place: 2.59--2.61, pp.58--59, scalar extension and splitting of restriction of scalars.

proof.text: Set $\chi_\sigma=\operatorname{pr}_\sigma$ in the split coordinates of Step 5. By the definition of $X^*$ in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], its underlying group is $\operatorname{Hom}_{k^s\text{-grp}}((Q_L)_{k^s},\mathbf G_m)$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices] over $k^s$, with source rank $|E|$ and target rank $1$ (choose any enumeration of the finite set $E$). Every character is uniquely $\prod_{\sigma\in E}\chi_\sigma^{m_\sigma}$, with $m_\sigma\in\mathbf Z$. The resulting isomorphism $\mathbf Z[E]\to X^*(Q_L)$ takes $e_\sigma$ to $\chi_\sigma$ and is independent of the enumeration, since this formula specifies it on every labelled basis vector.

source.place: Lemma 12.61, p.251; split character calculation, Theorem 12.9(b), pp.234--235.

proof.text:
Check the action by conjugation, as defined in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], on the coordinate functions themselves. The $\sigma$-coordinate linear form on $L\otimes_kk^s$ is $\lambda_\sigma(a\otimes b)=\sigma(a)b$. For $\gamma\in\Gamma$, conjugating this form gives
$$\bigl(\gamma\lambda_\sigma(1\otimes\gamma^{-1})\bigr)(a\otimes b)=\gamma\bigl(\sigma(a)\gamma^{-1}(b)\bigr)=(\gamma\circ\sigma)(a)b=\lambda_{\gamma\circ\sigma}(a\otimes b).$$
Equality holds on pure tensors and hence on their finite sums. Restriction to units gives equality of the regular coordinate characters, since they are restrictions of these linear forms on the affine space of $L$ used in Step 1. Thus $\gamma\chi_\sigma=\chi_{\gamma\circ\sigma}$ as scheme characters, not merely as functions on rational points. The map in Step 6 is therefore $\Gamma$-equivariant. If $L=k$, its basis has one element, $N(x)=x$, $Q_k=\mathbf G_m$, and the unique character basis vector is the identity character; all assertions include this case.

source.place: Lemma 12.61, p.251, equivariance of the embedding-indexed character basis.
